summary_paragraph: The patient, a paraplegic woman with a history of recurrent UTIs and pneumonias, was admitted for hypotension and respiratory failure following three days of lethargy and worsening dyspnea. She was intubated in the ED for acute respiratory failure due to healthcare-associated pneumonia and urosepsis from Citrobacter freundii. In the ICU, she developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) secondary to severe hypertension, presenting with headache and binocular blindness. MRI confirmed PRES, and blood pressure was controlled with hydralazine and chlorthalidone. She was extubated twice, with the second attempt successful after initial reintubation due to increased work of breathing. She completed a 14-day course of meropenem and gentamicin for UTI and a 7-day course of vancomycin for MRSA pneumonia. Her neurological symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home alert and breathing room air, with instructions to continue chlorthalidone and follow up with neurology and for repeat MRI in two weeks.
